BECAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT, SOYA BEAN OIL HAS RELEASED ONTO THE GROUND AND BALLAST. DURING THE INCIDENT POWER LINES AND POLES HAVE FALLEN ONTO THE AFFECTED CAR AND TRAIN. THERE HAS BEEN UNSPECIFIED DAMAGES, HOWEVER THE PRICE POINT FOR THOSE DAMAGES IS CURRENTLY UNKNOWN. BOTH MAINLINE TRACKS, THE YARD AT THE LOCATION, AND EL DORADO STREET HAVE BEEN BLOCKED OFF IN ALL DIRECTIONS. CURRENTLY IT IS UNKNOWN IF ANY PASSENGER TRAIN DELAYS HAVE OCCURRED. BECAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT AN ESTIMATED (16000) CUSTOMERS ARE WITHOUT POWER. AS A RESULT, THE UNPERMITTED ACROLEIN EMISSION HAS STOPPED WHILE THE PLANT IS DOWN. AN INVESTIGATION IS UNDERWAY TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE. *** INITIAL CONTINUOUS RELEASE REPORT ***

properties.title: NRC Report: Oil, Misc: Transformer in Roadside Ditch During Rain Event near Junction City, KS
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 978406 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: WESTAR ENERGY, INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 978406
Incident Time: 2011-06-02 09:30:00
Nearest City: Junction City, KS
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: OIL, MISC: TRANSFORMER
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: WESTAR ENERGY, INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
A LIGHTNING STRIKE AT THE JUNCTION CITY MAIN SUBSTATION CAUSED THE FAILURE OF A MAIN TRANSFORMER AND RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 100 GALLONS OF OIL. A SIGNIFICANT RAIN EVENT WAS OCCURRING AT THE TIME OF RELEASE AND RELEASED OIL WAS TRANSPORTED BEYOND THE FENCE OF THE SUBSTATION AND INTO A ROADSIDE DITCH. FAILURE OF THE TRANSFORMER SENT NOTIFICATION TO PERSONNEL WHO ARRIVED ON-SITE TO INVESTIGATE AND INITIAL CONTAINMENT BOOMS WERE PUT IN PLACE. TRANSFER OF OIL BEYOND THE INITIAL ROADSIDE DITCH WAS INITIALLY PREVENTED BY CONTAINMENT BOOMS AND SEDIMENT BLOCKING THE ROADSIDE CULVERTS. BY 07:30 AM A FULL RESPONSE TEAM WAS IN PLACE AND ADDITIONAL CONTAINMENT AND CLEAN-UP MATERIAL WAS DEPLOYED. CONTAINMENT AND RESPONSE WAS SUCCESSFUL IN PREVENTING THE RELEASE FROM EXPANDING BEYOND THE ROADSIDE DITCH IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT TO THE SUBSTATION.

properties.title: NRC Report: Unknown Material in Manayunk Canal near Philadelphia, PA
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 809559 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: RICHARDSAPEX
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 809559
Incident Time: 2006-08-29 13:30:00
Nearest City: Philadelphia, PA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: UNKNOWN MATERIAL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: RICHARDSAPEX
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 15 feet by 15 feet (area 225 sq. ft.)
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0.01 gallons
CALLER STATES THAT ON AUG 7TH, A DISCHARGE ON-SITE OF 2,700 GALLONS OF MINERAL OIL OCCURRED AT FACILITY, AND WAS CONTAINED IN CONCRETE FACILITY AREA. WHEN RESPONDERS CAME ON-SITE, THEY CONCLUDED MATERIAL WAS INDEED, CONTAINED AND DID NOT REACH WATER. HOWEVER, AFTER A FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION, NOT ALL 2,700 GALLONS WERE ACCOUNTED FOR. MARKEDLY, A CRACK WAS FOUND BETWEEN THE WALL AND THE FLOOR (WHERE MATERIAL MAY HAVE BEEN POCKETED). NO ACTUAL MATERIAL WAS SEEN GOING INTO THE MANAYUNK CANAL AT THIS TIME. HOWEVER, ALGAE POCKETS WERE DISCOVERED BY A 3RD PARTY CONSULTANT WHO CHECKED CLEAN-UP AT THIS TIME. LARGE AMOUNTS OF THE ALGAE WERE DISCOVERED IN THE CANAL, AND IT WAS DETERMINED THAT HEAVY RAINS RAISED THE HEIGHT OF THE CANAL THE NIGHT BEFORE, WASHING THE ALGAE POCKETS DOWNSTREAM INTO ANOTHER WATER SOURCE. AT THIS POINT IN TIME, AN UNKNOWN MATERIAL IS BEING RELEASED INTO THE CANAL NEAR FACILITY AND IS CREATING A SMALL RAINBOW SHEEN IN THE WATER. THE MATERIAL APPEARS TO COME UP IN SMALL DROPLET-SIZED PUFFS EVERY 5-10 MINUTES, AND IS ONLY SEEN DISCHARGING DURING PRODUCTION AT THE FACILITY. CALLER STATES THAT MATERIAL MAY BE COMING FROM VIBRATIONS OF PRODUCTION, BUT SOURCE AND CAUSE FOR MATERIAL RELEASE IS UNKNOWN. ADDITIONALLY, CALLER STATES THE DISCHARGE MAY BE COMING FROM AN INTERNAL STORAGE TANK FARM UNDER BEDROCK, AS SHE BELIEVES IT WASN'T DUG TOO DEEP.
